claim_boundary: The 48-match is an incidence-bus certificate, not a proof of graph isomorphism to the tomotope.
The 39=3*13 reading is a target for the qutrit crossover program; BT1711 only verifies the arithmetic layer split.

interpretive_payoff.axis_plus_yellow: 1+6 supplies the heptadic clock spine; the six yellow lines match the cyclic period of 1/7.
interpretive_payoff.gray_24: the 24 gray lines are the exact mutable sheet between skew and classical embeddings.
interpretive_payoff.red_blue_16_each: two 16-line domains supply dual 48-incidence buses, matching tomotope/Holonet timing.
interpretive_payoff.shared_39: 39=3*13 points toward the qutrit/Hesse projective closure as a crossover target, not yet an isomorphism.

summary: The q-2025 split-Cayley layering is not just decorative: relative to an axis, its 63 lines split as 1+6+24+16+16. The red and blue 16-line domains each carry a (24_2,16_3) incidence bus of size 48, exactly the same interface size as the tomotope middle layer and the Holonet 48-tick body. The skew/classical switch keeps 39 lines and changes precisely the 24 gray lines.
theorem: BT1711 Hexagon Layer / Tomotope Bus Theorem
